Deleting a recording asks first now.

The trash button on a library card, and the one on a timeline row, used to delete straight away — the audio, the transcript and the findings, with nothing to undo. Deleting a folder already asked, even though it only moves recordings; the more destructive action was the one that didn't. Both now open the same confirmation, with focus on Cancel. Removing a shared recording in an organisation says what it actually does: it goes away for everyone in the org, not just this machine.

Most of the rest of this release is Windows, where a lot of the desktop app had been built against macOS and shipped unchanged:

- **Deleting a folder works.** The folder came back, on disk and on screen, because the confirmation window made the app reload the cloud folder list mid-delete. The race behind it could also undo a folder edit on macOS if you switched away right after making it; local edits now win over an older cloud snapshot on both platforms.
- **A failed microphone no longer pretends to record.** With the mic denied, unplugged or held by another app, Start showed LIVE and a ticking clock, recorded nothing, and discarded the result at the end. It now reports the failure. The same fix closes two macOS cases where a recording could start with no working capture behind it.
- **Light mode shows headings again** in the debrief and the Ask panel — they were white on white, along with the findings table header. This affected macOS too.
- Settings and onboarding no longer claim that system audio is captured on Windows; it is not implemented there yet, and the "you dominated the conversation" score that came from its absence is gone.
- Shortcut keycaps, the maximize/restore button, window sizes on high-DPI displays, Traditional Chinese fonts, scrollbars, the right-click menu, exporting recordings whose titles contain `/` or `:`, copy to clipboard, and closing the window (it now quits) all behave like a Windows app.

Nothing changes on iOS or Android.
